column1: # What the Performance section of the root README charts: tools/readme/charts.py reads this file and benchmarks.tsv.
# Tab separated. Three kinds of line:
#     A chart, drawn once per OS that has data for it, to .github/assets/bench-<id>-<os>-{light,dark}.svg, in the
#     order of these lines. The README shows the Linux chart and puts the others in one <details>.
#     A row of a chart: the results of <benchmark> (Class.method) with exactly <params> (as benchmarks.tsv writes them,
#     the engine left out, "(none)" for no parameters), measured by the workflow group <group>. <metric> is what the
#     row compares: score (the JMH score: an engine's time per operation, or the inverse of its throughput), a counter
#     of benchmarks.tsv (bytes, lower is better), or the difference of two counters, a-b. <label> is the row's title,
#     short: the chart prints Ledger's result beside it.
#     <metric> does not compare engines on <os> (ubuntu-latest, windows-latest or macos-latest): the rows that chart it
#     show <reason> in place of their bars on that OS.
# A result worth stating, a loss above all, is charted as a row, never written out as text beside the charts. Every
# result, charted or not, is in benchmarks.tsv; benchmark/README.md describes every workload.
